description.en: The PosiFit ontology is intended to describe positive-energy building retrofit projects. It is designed around the reuse and alignment of established domain ontologies. BOT is used for spatial structure, SAREF for devices and measurements, Brick for point roles and timeseries references, QUDT for units, and vCard and WGS84 for addresses and coordinates. Terms are introduced in the pf: namespace only where a concept is not covered by these existing vocabularies. This documentation therefore focuses on the PosiFit-specific classes and properties, together with the alignments that connect them to the ontologies they reuse.

abstract.value: A vocabulary for describing positive-energy building retrofits. It covers the spatial breakdown of a monitored site and the sensing equipment, measurement points and timeseries references attached to it.

definition.value: A single enclosed room within a dwelling.
A power conversion unit serving a PV array and a battery together, converting between the DC of both and the AC of the building supply.
Whether a window stands open or closed.
Signed instantaneous power at a battery system, positive while charging and negative while discharging.
Energy stored in a battery system as a fraction of the energy it holds when full.
A sensor mounted in a dwelling space, measuring indoor air temperature, relative humidity and CO2 concentration.
Luminous flux per unit area incident on a surface at a site.
A device measuring a physical property of a building space.
A device mounted on a radiator, estimating the heat the radiator gives off from its surface temperature and the room air temperature, and counting it in units used to split a shared heating bill.
Target air temperature a controlling device works towards.
A thermostatic radiator valve with a motorised actuator and an onboard radio, throttling the flow through one radiator against a temperature setpoint and measuring the conditions in the room.
An electricity meter of a dwelling unit, measuring active power and active energy.
A self-contained dwelling unit on a floor, billed and monitored separately.
Electric potential difference at a metering point.
A device at a site measuring the outdoor conditions a building is exposed to.
A location containing one or more buildings, georeferenced by a zero point.
A room of a dwelling containing a bath or shower, and usually a washbasin and a toilet.
A photovoltaic installation on a building, converting incident solar radiation into electricity fed to the building or to storage.
Speed of the air moving past a site.
A space held under a single tenancy.
An electrochemical storage installation serving a building, charging from the supply or from on-site generation and discharging back into it.
Cumulative electrical energy delivered by an on-site generation system.
Cumulative electrical energy consumed by a unit.
Cumulative electrical energy a battery system has taken in.
Power oscillating between source and reactive load at a metering point, doing no net work.
A horizontal level of a building, containing the spaces at that height.
A study-bedroom in a student residence, sharing sanitary and cooking facilities with the floor.
Temperature of the heat-emitting surface of a radiator.
Frequency of the alternating supply at a metering point.
Heat given off by a radiator over a billing period, counted in the dimensionless units of a heat cost allocator.
An openable glazed opening in the envelope of a space.
Remaining charge of a device's battery as a fraction of its capacity.
Instantaneous electrical power drawn by a unit.
Dry-bulb temperature of the outdoor air at a site.
Product of RMS voltage and RMS current at a metering point, the vector sum of active and reactive power.
Electric current flowing through a metering point.
An independent structure with a roof and walls, containing dwellings and building systems.
A contact sensor mounted on a window, measuring whether it stands open or closed.
A room of a dwelling used for preparing food.
A named stream of measurements produced by a device for one quantity, carrying a reference to the timeseries held outside the graph.
Concentration of carbon dioxide in the air of a space.
Cumulative electrical energy a battery system has given back.
Instantaneous electrical power delivered by an on-site generation system.
Nameplate energy a storage system holds when full, as declared by its manufacturer.
Ratio of active to apparent power at a metering point, between zero and one.
Ratio of the water vapour present in the air to the amount that would saturate it at the same temperature.
Whether the radiator a valve controls is calling for heat.
Dry-bulb temperature of air.
Cumulative electrical energy a unit has fed back into the supply.
Degree to which a valve stands open, from fully closed to fully open.
Dry-bulb temperature of the air inside a space.
A panel-mounted electricity meter, measuring what a consumption meter does and, in addition, voltage, current, frequency, reactive power, apparent power and power factor.
Links a measurement point to the quantity its stream carries.
Billing period a measurement point's count covers, relative to the present.
Code identifying a tenant space within its site.
Nameplate energy capacity of a storage system, in kilowatt-hours.
Short code identifying a site.
